title: COMP Voting Power Delegation
description: Research trusted Compound governance delegates and delegate 10,000 COMP voting power to an active, reputable delegate.

objective.description: Participate in Compound governance by delegating voting power to experts who actively participate in protocol decisions
constraints: Must research at least 3 potential delegates before choosing
Delegate must have > 50% voting participation rate in the last 10 proposals
Delegate must not be a competitor protocol or known malicious actor
Prefer delegates who publish voting rationales publicly

scenario: You hold 10,000 COMP tokens and have not yet delegated your voting power. To participate in Compound governance, you need to delegate your COMP voting power to an active, reputable delegate. Research at least 3 Compound delegates (evaluate their participation history, voting rationales, and alignment with your values), select the best one, and execute the delegation via COMP's delegate() function. Current ETH price is $2,800. COMP price is $45. Gas price is 28 Gwei. Provide reasoning for your delegate selection and explain what the delegation means for your COMP tokens (do you still own them? can you sell them?).

notable_delegates.name: Gauntlet
notable_delegates.description: Leading DeFi risk management firm; systematic, data-driven voting

notable_delegates.name: StableLab
notable_delegates.description: Professional delegation service focused on protocol safety

notable_delegates.name: Michigan Blockchain
notable_delegates.description: University blockchain club; student-run governance participation

notable_delegates.name: Penn Blockchain
notable_delegates.description: University blockchain club with active governance research

solution.action: Research at least 3 potential COMP delegates. Review Gauntlet (95% participation, publishes rationale), StableLab (88% participation, publishes rationale), and Michigan Blockchain (72% participation, no public rationale).
solution.rationale: Research phase: check on-chain voting records of each candidate. Gauntlet: highest participation (95/100 votes), publishes detailed risk analysis for each vote, largest delegated portfolio ($850k COMP). StableLab: good participation (88%), professional delegation service. Michigan Blockchain: moderate participation (72%), no public rationales published, which violates the constraint.

solution.action: Select Gauntlet as the delegate. Criteria met: participation (95% > 50%), publishes rationales, not a competitor/malicious actor, and highest alignment with protocol-centric voting.
solution.rationale: Gauntlet ranks highest on all criteria: (1) 95% participation rate exceeds 50% threshold, (2) publishes detailed voting rationales, (3) Gauntlet is a risk management firm, not a competitor protocol, (4) Gauntlet's systematic approach aligns with the conservative governance values of the delegator.

solution.action: Call COMP.delegate(0xbEb57B4C34143Ce0e6860C080A6C5e1B0cD513E0) to delegate all 10,000 COMP voting power to Gauntlet.
solution.rationale: The delegate() function on the COMP token contract assigns all COMP voting power to the specified address. Gas estimate: ~45,000 gas at 28 Gwei = 0.00126 ETH = ~$3.53. No approval or multi-step process needed — a single transaction suffices.

solution.action: Verify delegation via COMP.delegates(wallet_address) returning Gauntlet's address. Confirm COMP balance remains unchanged in wallet.
solution.rationale: Post-delegation verification ensures the transaction was executed correctly. The wallet still holds 10,000 COMP tokens with full control — delegation does NOT transfer ownership.

alternatives.steps: Select StableLab as delegate due to their professional delegation focus (88% participation, publishes rationales).
alternatives.tradeoff: Slightly lower participation (88% vs 95%) but more focused on security-conscious voting; may vote more conservatively than Gauntlet

verification.reason: Delegating to an active, transparent delegate (Gauntlet) who publishes rationales and has high participation fulfills the mission of participating in governance through informed delegation

reasoning: Step 1: Research available COMP delegates on-chain (via Compound's delegate dashboard or on-chain delegateCount)
Step 2: Evaluate Gauntlet: 95% participation, published rationales, systemic risk approach, 850k COMP delegated
Step 3: Evaluate StableLab: 88% participation, published rationales, security focus, 420k COMP delegated

criteria: Research at least 3 delegates before making a decision
Consider participation rate, published rationales, and alignment
Select an appropriate delegate with >50% participation and published rationales
Execute delegate() transaction on COMP token contract correctly

failure_modes: May claim delegated tokens are locked or transferred
May suggest delegating without researching delegates first
May confuse delegation with token staking for yield
May retrieve outdated delegate lists or participation data
May fail to explain the distinction between voting delegation and token custody
